tldr: A beginner lab on building AI agents in Java with LangChain4j and CDI: AI services, memory, function calling, agent workflows and the Supervisor pattern.
summary: Part 1 treats AI as a service: attendees inject LLM-backed services through CDI like any other bean, manage conversational memory with scopes such as @SessionScoped, and give agents tools through function calling.

Part 2 moves to agent architecture: designing declarative sequential and parallel workflows and the Supervisor pattern, where an AI plans and manages other agents. The lab also aims to give attendees a grasp of the MCP and A2A protocols and patterns for integrating agents into enterprise architectures.
keyPoints: AI services are injected via CDI using LangChain4j.
Conversational memory is managed with scopes such as @SessionScoped.
Sequential and parallel workflows and the Supervisor pattern for agents.
Introduction to MCP and A2A protocols.
takeaways: Expose one existing Java service as a tool an LLM agent can call.
watchIf: You are a Java developer wanting a first hands-on path into building agents.
